survey: A stylised ringed planet (Saturn-like) floating against a purple striped background. Main parts: (1) An orange sphere with a cream band across its upper half and a second cream/orange band near the bottom. It has a few small crater dots, is roughly round and is tilted slightly toward the viewer. (2) One flat yellow ring with some thickness, tilted at the same angle as the bands and centred on the sphere. The near half of the ring crosses in front of the sphere's lower middle. The far half goes behind the sphere: it shows at upper right, and at left you can see purple through the gap between ring and sphere. The sphere's bottom shows below the front of the ring, and its outline continues as a sphere should. The ring never touches the sphere, which is correct for planetary rings, so the gap is not a missing support. Nothing is attached, hanging or resting on a surface, and a planet floating in space needs no support.
